title: Supply chain hardening (npm hygiene + Claude Code hooks)
description: Harden the npm dependency surface and add the first Claude Code hooks for the harness. Motivated by the recent wave of npm supply-chain incidents (compromised maintainer accounts publishing malicious postinstall scripts, e.g. the s1ngularity / chalk-debug class of attacks). Adds three defensive layers: (1) `.npmrc` with `ignore-scripts=true`, `engine-strict=true`, and `minimum-release-age=7d` (npm 11.7+) — blocks the dominant attack vector and the recently-published-package window; (2) `npm audit` step in `init.sh` failing on moderate-or-higher, with the current 5 transitive CVEs resolved via `npm audit fix` and `overrides` where needed; (3) `.claude/settings.json` with hooks blocking out-of-band edits to `feature_list.json` and `package-lock.json`. Also pins Node/npm versions via `engines`, adds Dependabot config, documents the policy in `docs/conventions.md`, and updates `CHECKPOINTS.md`. Inserted at priority 0.5 — before `test-baseline` — so every subsequent feature inherits the hardening. RE-OPENED 2026-05-19 after the initial close: the Claude Code hooks shipped using a non-existent env var (`CLAUDE_TOOL_INPUT_FILE_PATH`) and therefore never blocked anything. The reviewer's verification was synthetic (set the variable manually and confirmed the bash branch executed) but not end-to-end (never confirmed that Claude Code actually populates that variable). The correct mechanism is stdin JSON parsed via `jq` against `.tool_input.file_path`. This re-open ships the corrected hook, adds a real end-to-end verification recipe to `reviewer.md`, and updates `leader.md` to reflect that status rotations in `feature_list.json` will go through `jq`-driven Bash from now on (the hook will block direct Edit|Write).
acceptance: `.npmrc` exists with `ignore-scripts=true`, `engine-strict=true`, `minimum-release-age=7d`, and a comment block documenting the rationale for each setting.

An allowlist mechanism exists for legitimate postinstall scripts (esbuild today). Approach is documented in `docs/conventions.md` — current preferred form: explicit `npm rebuild esbuild` step in `init.sh` after `npm ci --ignore-scripts`.

`init.sh` adds: (a) `npm --version >= 11.7` sanity check, (b) explicit `npm ci` with `ignore-scripts` honoured (relies on `.npmrc`), (c) `npm rebuild` for the allowlisted packages, (d) `npm audit --audit-level=moderate` step failing the build on findings.

title: Fix GitHub Pages deploy after engine-strict policy
description: After feature 0.5 (supply-chain-hardening) introduced `engines: { node: '>=20', npm: '>=11.7' }` in package.json plus `engine-strict=true` in .npmrc, the GitHub Pages deploy workflow started failing on `npm ci` with EBADENGINE. The runner installs Node 20.18 (per .nvmrc) which ships with npm 10.8.2 — below the 11.7 floor we require. The fix is a single step in `.github/workflows/deploy-frontend.yml` that bumps npm to 11.x immediately after `actions/setup-node`. title: Code-split routes with React.lazy + Suspense
description: The bundle has grown to 680.84 KB through the major dep bumps (vite/plugin-react, eslint, react). Vite's 500 KB warning fires on every build. This feature lazy-loads the heavy routes (`/new` NewGame and `/play` Play) with React.lazy + <Suspense>, dropping the initial bundle well below 500 KB and putting per-route chunks in dist/assets/. The WIP pages (/home, /login, /about) stay eager because they're trivial — splitting them would add chunk-loading overhead with no payload benefit. Inserted at priority 3.92 immediately after react-major-bump (3.9) — does bundle hygiene before any further code addition (especially the deferred react-chessboard 4→5 bump which would add ~50 KB to whatever chunk Play lives in).
acceptance: src/routes/Public.tsx imports NewGame and Play via React.lazy(() => import(...)) instead of eager imports. Error and WIP stay eager.

A <Suspense fallback={...}/> boundary wraps the lazy outlet. Fallback uses MUI components consistent with the rest of the app (likely a centered <CircularProgress />). Lives either in App.tsx around <Outlet /> or in Public.tsx as the route element wrapper — implementer picks the cleaner spot.

Existing tests still pass (49 expected). Tests that render NewGame or Play directly (via MemoryRouter etc.) may need an outer <Suspense> wrapper or await-style queries (findBy...) — implementer applies the minimum tweak needed. No tests removed or skipped.
dist/assets/ now contains at least 3 JS chunks: an initial chunk (App shell + theme + router + WIP page), a NewGame chunk, a Play chunk. Implementer reports the sizes.
Initial chunk drops well below 500 KB (no Vite chunk-size warning on the initial). Per-route chunks may individually be above their own thresholds but that's the point — they only load on navigation.
Total bundle size (sum of all JS chunks) should be roughly the same as before, possibly slightly larger due to chunk boundaries (small overhead). ±20 KB tolerance on the sum.
Dev server (`npm run dev`) and HMR still work end-to-end. Navigating between /home, /new, /play in the dev server triggers the lazy loads without stalls or crashes.

title: Bump react-chessboard 4 → 5 (semantic API migration)
description: Apply Dependabot PR #9 (react-chessboard 4.7.3 → 5.10.0). Unlike the other dep bumps in this series, this one requires a real semantic migration in pages/Play.tsx because the v4 → v5 transition collapsed the individual props (position, onPieceDrop, boardOrientation, areArrowsAllowed) into a single `options` object, renamed `areArrowsAllowed` to `allowDrawingArrows`, and changed the `onPieceDrop` callback signature from `(source, target) => boolean` to `({ piece, sourceSquare, targetSquare }) => boolean` with `targetSquare` now nullable (drag-off-board). The underlying DnD backend was also swapped from react-dnd to `@dnd-kit/core` + `@dnd-kit/modifiers`, adding ~50-80 KB to whatever chunk the chessboard lives in. Thanks to code-splitting-routes (3.92), that growth falls into the `/play` lazy chunk (currently 144.72 KB) and does NOT affect the 470.99 KB initial-load surface.
